text.p: Bonds closed higher, driven along by the Bunds, and traders expected the longer end to match any gains by the German market on Friday.
The strength of the longer end led to some slight flattening of the curve.
"The Bund was in the driving seat. It rose and pushed all Europe up. Italy, which has a wider spread, obviously had more room to gain than we did," said one trader.
"The 10 years are still strong and are not going to lose any ground on the Bund tomorrow. Germany will call the tune," added another trader.

"If the (Bund) futures breaks the figure (103), then our futures will test the next resistance at 111.25," said one chart analyst. "From that point, the 10 year (cash) will go quickly to 6.20 percent," he added.
Traders said that liquidity was probably going to be slightly less on Friday, with the market starting to look forward to the French audit of state finances due on Monday.

There could also be some steepening of the curve after the heavy concentration on the longer end on Thursday, traders added. The spread between the March 1999 and the February 2007 narrowed to 106 basis points from 110 on Wednesday.
